fact: The Ministry of Justice says lawyers can obtain copies of judgments and submit service and enforcement requests through the Lawyer platform, launched with Casablanca courts.
Morocco's justice minister says an electronic judicial case file, to digitise all case files of every type and jurisdiction, is being prepared.
Morocco's justice minister says lawyers can now file requests, briefs and appeal acts through a dedicated platform.
The Ministry of Justice says its lawyer electronic-exchange platform lets lawyers file pleadings with the chosen court and pay court fees online, the filing going straight to the court.
The Mahakim file-tracking service lets the public follow civil and criminal files, notifications, enforcement and recovery files, and hearing dates by entering the file number at the court.

The justice minister told the House of Representatives on 2 November 2026 the ministry is speeding court digitisation, generalising the electronic case file and digital notification, and creating a national platform for enforcing judgments, at about MAD 2.5 billion to complete.

Justice Minister Abdellatif Ouahbi told a parliamentary committee that a national enforcement platform, letting enforcement files be processed nationally and not only in Casablanca, has entered implementation and is being extended to all courts.
Village de la Justice says ICT give Moroccan magistrates and clerks instant access to files and real-time tracking, with the Ministry of Justice's mahakim.ma as the main e-justice platform.
Village de la Justice says the Ministry of Justice's mahakim.ma app lets citizens follow the processing of their cases remotely.
